messages:
maria: Heads-up: hit a goroutine leak in Go SDK generator when the ctx passed to NewGenerator cancels during handshake. Repro in our auth-refresh sample app where we short timeout the ctx.
aj: can you paste the minimal repro and sdk version?
maria: using v0.13.2 (vendored). minimal repro looks like:
```
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 50*time.Millisecond)
gen, err := client.NewGenerator(ctx, model, opts...)
// call gen.Stream or gen.Next immediately after constructor
```
if ctx times out during the handshake we observe a goroutine stuck reading from the socket.
ryan: I think NewGenerator spins up the read loop before handshake completion and doesn't stop it if constructor returns error/cancel.
aj: that matches a convo i remember. quick patch idea: don't start the read goroutine until handshake has finished successfully.
maria: tried locally: moving start of read loop to after handshake finishes avoids leak. also adding a select on ctx.Done() in constructor prevents spinning.
ryan: good find. sounds like we need a unit test that cancels during handshake to prevent regressions.
aj: agree. also add a note in SDK docs about what ctx controls. Python/JS SDKs already gate read loop on handshake; go is inconsistent.
maria: question: should constructor accept two contexts (handshake ctx vs lifecycle ctx)? changing signature is breaking. maybe do small fix now + RFC for API change.
ryan: yep minimal fix + test, then follow up RFC if we want to expose separate lifecycle control. open PR with label "generator: handshake-cancel-leak" and add me + aj as reviewers. post to eng-runtime and devex for visibility.
ciaran-bot: CI triggered for PR #5432 — running tests (1 retry allowed for flaky runner) :robot_face:
maria: will open PR in the next hour, adding the test + fix. thanks! :thumbsup:
